v.why: Removing edge 5 when edge 3 is already none cuts the input-output path and collapses accuracy (-76/-62/-27), while with edge 3 present the same edit costs under 1 point on C10.
Adding a conv to an empty direct input-output edge creates a new path and gives large gains, whereas replacing an existing op gives smaller changes.
Replacing none with skip restores a direct path (+4 to +16), whereas replacing a conv with skip loses capacity (e.g. -6/-13/-13).
Swapping a 3x3 conv for skip throws away capacity (-2.5/-4.7/-10), while filling a none edge with skip tends to help.
Replacing a 3x3 conv on the middle edge with skip reduces accuracy on all datasets, whereas replacing a 1x1 conv is roughly neutral.
Upgrading a skip to a 3x3 conv on edge 2 gave consistent gains on all three datasets, while filling a none edge gave inconsistent or negligible changes.
Replacing a weak avg_pool at the input edge with a conv gives large gains across datasets, bigger than conv-for-conv or 1x1 upgrades.
Removing a pooling edge helps (+14.8/+17.7/+0.6), whereas removing a conv edge hurts.
Upgrading a skip on the output edge to a 3x3 conv gives consistent gains across datasets, larger than filling a none edge.
Replacing a skip on edge 1 with a conv adds capacity on a path that otherwise has none, while adding one to a none edge is near zero.
